surfaces.part: packed-earth ground patch with oil blotches

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a full 64-wide, 48-row rectangle (width 64 on every row). The column scans show only mottled brown dirt tones (L about 100-108) with a few small dark or grey sheen pixels. No row carries a front-edge line, eave shadow, or a separate vertical face. The image is a uniform top-down ground texture with dark blotches near rows 4-9, 19-27 and 35-42, so there is no front face (0 rows). This matches a flat decal seen from above, which reads as a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate shows 5 visible tones per tile. That is above the grass reference (3) and below the paving reference (7), so it is within the range of the references. Near-flat coverage is 0%, and the packed-earth ground carries dithered speckle and grain, so there are no flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the dark blotch tones lean brown rather than being a black sticker outline. The soaked-brown edge is dithered into the dirt instead of being drawn as a hard line. The ramp (dirt, soaked brown, dark brown, black-brown core, grey-violet sheen) gives about 5 steps, which is close to the references. Texture is somewhat sparser than the grass clumps, which is why I rate it 'some' rather than 'rich'. It reads as a coherent ground patch of the same kind and scale as the references.
